She [[Type expert|specializes]] in {{type|Bug}} {{OBP|Pokémon|species}}. She hands out the {{badge|PaldeaBug|Bug Badge}} to {{pkmn|Trainer}}s who defeat her. ==In the core series games== Besides being a Gym Leader, Katy runs a bakery named Patisserie Soapberry (Japanese: '''パティスリー　ムクロジ''' ''Pâtisserie Mukuroji''), having inherited the shop from her family.[[Magazines in the Pokémon world|Sweet Truth!]]: ''"At the heart of it all is Katy, the proprietor, who inherited the [Patisserie Soapberry] from family and keeps its ovens hard at work!"'' ({{pkmn|Scarlet and Violet}}) She believes that both sweets and Bug-type Pokémon have great power despite their small sizes.[https://scarletviolet.pokemon.com/en-us/characters/katy/ Katy — Pokémon Scarlet and Pokémon Violet | Official Website] She was trained in the art of baking under the wing of [[Kofu]]. Because her Gym is so close to [[Mesagoza]], where many Trainers begin their [[Pokémon journey]], [[Geeta]] urges Katy to keep her battle style light and easy despite her wanting to go more all out, as evident by her Gym having the lowest-leveled Pokémon in the [[Paldea League]]. After her post-game [[rematch]] with the {{player}}, she has a moment of reflection and decides to step up the difficulty of her Gym to fit her style more. In addition to the Gym Badge, Katy gives out {{TM|021|Pounce}} after defeating her. concept art | colspan=2 | Eyecatch |} ==In animation== ===''Pokémon Horizons: The Series''=== [[File:Katy anime.png|thumb|250px|Katy in {{aniseries|HZ}}]] ====History==== Katy appeared in silhouette alongside the other Gym Leaders in ''[[HZ046|Welcome to Naranja Academy!]]'', and was later mentioned as [[Liko]]'s first challenge at [[Tera Training]]. Katy physically debuted in ''[[HZ047|Put Your Heart Into It!]]'' as the owner of Patisserie Soapberry, where [[Murdock]] was working for the time being. Katy set a baking contest between Liko and [[Coral]] to see which one of them would battle her, which Liko won, allowing Liko to battle her. After Coral threw a tantrum over her loss, Katy gave her a stern scolding and intimidating stare which made Coral leave without further incident. Although Liko lost the battle, Katy gave her a passing mark as she had mastered the basics of Terastallizing. In ''[[HZ055|Showdown! The Paldea Elite Four]]'', Katy appeared at [[Naranja Academy]] to act as Liko's partner against [[Rika]] in the [[Elite Four Tag Battle]]. In [[HZ056|the following episode]], Katy played the role of support by having her {{p|Lokix}} protect Liko's Floragato from taking damage. When Lokix ended up {{status|poison}}ed, Katy stopped holding back and had Lokix launch a barrage of attacks to both damage and weaken Rika's Pokémon before succumbing to its status ailment. Despite this, Rika's {{p|Clodsire}} eventually defeated Floragato, winning the battle. Afterward, Katy consoled an emotional Liko, who began crying from the frustration of losing despite giving it her all in battle. In ''[[HZ067|Shine on, Terastallization! Liko vs. Roy!]]'', Katy met up with Liko along with Ann to encourage Liko before her battle against Roy, Katy then watched the match unfold. After the battle, Katy and Grusha met up with Liko to encourage her on her progress as a Trainer. In ''[[HZ096|Crash! Team Dragon Rampage!]]'', Dot revealed that after the [[Rising Volt Tacklers]] disbanded, Murdock went back to working for Katy at the Patisserie Soapberry. In ''[[HZ098|Reunion in Cortondo]]'', Katy and Murdock met with Liko, Roy, Dot, and their new traveling companion, [[Ult]]. Upon learning the children reformed the Rising Volt Tacklers, Murdock grew concerned for their safety. Katy helped relieve Murdock's worries by having a rematch with Liko to show how much she had grown. She revealed her {{p|Teddiursa|Teddy}} had [[Evolution|Evolved]] into a {{p|Ursaring}} and used it to battle [[Pagogo]], which eventually ended in Liko's victory. Afterward, as she and Murdock saw the children off, Katy praised them for continuing to grow despite the hardships they faced. She then suggested that Murdock also had potential to grow, proposing that he rejoin Liko and the others when the time was right. In ''[[HZ100|We Are the Rising Volt Tacklers!]]'', Katy was shown in a flashback, saying goodbye to Murdock as he left to rejoin the Rising Volt Tacklers. ====Character==== Katy has a kind and upbeat personality, being friendly to people she meets. However, when people are misbehaving or causing trouble in front of her like with Coral, she becomes more strict and fierce, not being afraid to tell people off. In battle Katy becomes more excited and ruthless, she loves going all out and does not like holding back against opponents, like with her battle against Rika. ====Pokémon==== =====On hand===== {{TrainerPoké |trainer=Katy |nick=Teddy |tera=Bug |type1=Normal |img=Katy Teddy.png |cap=Katy's Ursaring |img2=Katy Teddy Terastal.png |cap2=Katy's Terastallized Ursaring |epnum=HZ047 |epname=Put Your Heart Into It! |vajp=Kei Shindō |vajpnote=as Teddiursa |vajp2=Taku Yashiro |vajp2note=as Ursaring |vaen= |desc={{p|Ursaring|Teddy}} (Japanese: '''クマちゃん''' ''Kuma-chan'') is Katy's first known Pokémon and first appeared as a {{p|Teddiursa}}. It is capable of {{Tera}}stallizing into a {{t|Bug}} type. Katy used it in her battle against [[Liko]] and her {{TP|Liko|Floragato}}. Despite Liko Terastallizing her Floragato, Teddy was ultimately able to overwhelm and defeat her. It reappeared during a flashback in ''[[HZ063|Ice Battle! Cold-Eyed Grusha]]''. In ''[[HZ098|Reunion in Cortondo]]'', it was shown to have evolved into an Ursaring. Katy used it in her [[rematch]] against Liko, where it battled [[Pagogo]], only to be defeated. Teddy reappeared during a flashback in ''[[HZ100|We Are the Rising Volt Tacklers!]]'', when Murdock revealed he was leaving to rejoin the Rising Volt Tacklers. Teddy's known moves are {{m|Charm}}, {{m|Slash}}, {{m|Sweet Scent}}, {{m|Fury Cutter}}, {{m|High Horsepower}}, and {{m|Hammer Arm}}.}} {{TrainerPoké |trainer=Katy |pkmn=Lokix |type1=Bug |type2=Dark |img=Katy Lokix.png |epnum=HZ055 |epname=Showdown! None of Teddiursa's moves are known.}} ==In the TCG== [[File:KatyScarletViolet237.jpg|200px|thumb|Ultra rare Katy]] {{main|Katy (Scarlet & Violet 177)}} '''Katy''' was introduced as a {{TCG|Supporter card}} in the [[Pokémon Trading Card Game]] during the English Scarlet & Violet Series (the Japanese Scarlet & Violet Era). It was first released in the Japanese {{TCG|Violet ex}} expansion and the English {{TCG|Scarlet & Violet}} expansion, with artwork by [[Akira Komayama]]. An {{TCG|ultra rare}} version of the card with artwork by the same illustrator was also included in these sets. It lets players shuffle their hand into their deck, and draw eight cards. This ends the player's turn. {{-}} ==Trivia== [[File:SV Reveal Trailer Katy Apron.png|thumb|250px|An apron with the earlier unused design for Katy's logo, as seen in the {{g|Scarlet and Violet}} reveal trailer.]] * Katy's Japanese Gym Leader title is {{tt|お菓子の虫|Bug of Sweets}}. * The spider web logo on Katy's apron is notably different in her concept art compared to her final design — the unused logo has a more elaborate look, with a depiction of a slice of cake in one section of the web. An apron with the unused logo is shown prominently in the announcement trailer for {{g|Scarlet and Violet}}.[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=MAmueMsFR1o Pokémon Scarlet and Pokémon Violet | Announcement Trailer - YouTube] * Katy has the highest [[Trainer ID number]] (993663) of any NPC in the franchise whose ID number is canonically known, as seen in the [[in-game trade]] she offers in Blueberry Academy's League Club Room. * Katy is the only [[Paldea]] Gym Leader whose Terastallized Pokémon changes between her initial Gym battle and her rematch battle (due to her {{p|Teddiursa}} having [[Evolution|evolved]] into {{p|Ursaring}}). ** The fact that Katy's Terastallized Pokémon is Teddiursa (and later Ursaring) may allude to common depictions of bears enjoying honey. It may also be a pun on the {{wp|bugbear}}, a mythical creature. ** She is also the only [[Non-player character|NPC]] {{pkmn|Trainer}} to use a Terastallized Pokémon that is not fully evolved in her final team, as Ursaring is unable to evolve into {{p|Ursaluna}} in Scarlet and Violet. ** Along with [[Hassel]], Katy is also the other Trainer to use a non-fully evolved Pokémon in their [[League Club Room]] team. * Katy's hairstyle and the pattern of her hat resemble insects' antennae, while her tight-fitting clothing with a waistband around her body bears a resemblance to an insect's segmented body. * Katy was designed by [[Megumi Mizutani]].[https://twitter.com/megtany/status/1984426148626133440 Twitter post about designing Katy, Brassius, Iono, and Tulip] ==Names== {| class="roundtable" style="background:#{{bug color}}; border:3px solid #{{bug color dark}}" |- ! style="background:#{{bug color light}}" | Language ! style="background:#{{bug color light}}" | Name ! style="background:#{{bug color light}}" | Origin |- | Japanese | カエデ ''Kaede'' | From 楓 ''kaede'' ({{wp|maple}}) |- | English | Katy | Similar to her Japanese name and possibly from ''{{wp|Tettigoniidae|katydid}}'' (bush crickets) |- | German | Ronah | From an anagram of ''Ahorn'' (maple) |- | European Spanish,
